extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on handling appeals before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, including admissibility of affidavits/declarations after appeal, remands for consideration or further search, new grounds of rejection, rehearing requests, and examiner actions following Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits or declarations filed after appeal (37 CFR 1.195)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations, or exhibits submitted after the case has been appealed will not be admitted without a showing of good and sufficient reasons why they were not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations filed with or after filing a notice of appeal but before jurisdiction passes to the Board will be considered for entry only if appellant makes the necessary showing under 37 CFR 1.195; Board authority is not necessary in that window. Affidavits/declarations filed after the application has been forwarded to the Board but before a Board decision cannot be considered by the examiner absent a remand by the Board. On remand the examiner will consider the affidavit/declaration only if accompanied by the showing required under 37 CFR 1.195; otherwise the examiner will not consider its merits. If delay in filing is satisfactorily explained, the examiner will admit and consider it. It is not customary for the Board to remand affidavits/declarations offered in connection with a request for rehearing where no rejection under 37 CFR 1.196(b) has been made; such submissions are then considered only as arguments (In re Martin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand by Board to examiner to consider affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: When affidavits or declarations are filed after the application has been forwarded to the Board but before a decision, the examiner lacks authority to consider them in the absence of a remand by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On remand the examiner should consider the affidavits/declarations as facts in the case require, return the application with a supplemental examiner's answer, and forward a copy to appellant. If the affidavit/declaration lacks the showing required under 37 CFR 1.195, the examiner will not consider its merits; if delay is satisfactorily explained the examiner will admit and consider it. Remand to consider a response relating to a 37 CFR 1.196(b) rejection is handled under MPEP §1214.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand by Board for further search
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be rare for the Board to remand a case to the examiner for further search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A remand extends total pendency and may necessitate a patent term extension under 35 U.S.C. 154(b). When remand for further search is necessary, the Board should conduct a search (on-line or otherwise) of at least one subclass and cite art from that subclass to demonstrate the basis on which it concludes a search of this area would be productive. The cited art need not be art upon which a rejection can be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may require appellant to address matters (37 CFR 1.196(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may require appellant to address any matter deemed appropriate for a reasoned decision on the pending appeal; appellant will be given a non-extendable time period to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include applicability of particular case law or prior art not previously identified. Failure to respond within the time set will result in dismissal of the appeal. The making of such a requirement is discretionary and does not affect the Board's authority to remand; after an appellant replies remand to the examiner may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision outcomes and nonfinality when remand included (37 CFR 1.196(a),(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may affirm or reverse the examiner's decision in whole or in part on the grounds and claims specified, or remand the application to the examiner; a decision that includes or allows a remand is not a final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmance of the rejection of a claim on any grounds specified constitutes a general affirmance except as to grounds specifically reversed. After proceedings on remand, the Board may enter an order making its decision final or render a new decision based on all appealed claims as appropriate. Board decisions sometimes set forth a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement that claim may be allowed in amended form (37 CFR 1.196(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board's decision includes an explicit statement that a claim may be allowed in amended form, appellant has the right to amend in conformity with such statement and the statement is binding on the examiner in the absence of new references or grounds of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board's making of such a statement is discretionary. A mere remark that a certain feature does not appear in a claim is not to be taken as a statement that the claim may be allowed if the feature is supplied by amendment (Ex parte Norlund). The right to amend in conformity with a 1.196(c) statement may only be exercised within the period allowed for seeking court review under 37 CFR 1.304; see MPEP §1216.

rubrics_metrics.name: New ground(s) of rejection by the Board (37 CFR 1.196(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board has knowledge of any grounds not involved in the appeal for rejecting any pending claim, it may include a statement to that effect with reasons — which constitutes a new ground of rejection and is not final for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Board makes a new ground of rejection, the appellant, within two months from the decision date, must either (1) submit an appropriate amendment of the claims and/or a showing of facts to have the matter reconsidered by the examiner (resulting in remand), or (2) request rehearing under §1.197(b). The new ground of rejection may apply to claims including allowed claims; Board authorization to reject allowed claims is discretionary and not a mandate to reexamine every allowed claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate amendment or showing under 37 CFR 1.196(b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment is 'appropriate' if it amends one or more of the claims rejected or substitutes new claims to avoid the art or reasons adduced by the Board; such amended or new claims must be directed to the same subject matter as the appealed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding new claims without amending or substituting for the rejected claims is not appropriate — new claims will not be entered and the amendment may be treated as a request for rehearing if it contains argument concerning the Board's rejection. A 'showing of facts' may be a showing under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131 or 1.132. If appellant submits argument without an appropriate amendment/showing it will be treated as a request for rehearing. If the examiner does not consider the amendment/showing to overcome the rejection, the examiner will again reject the claims (possibly finally). If a final rejection results and further review is desired, a new appeal is required limited to the new ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for rehearing of new ground or decision (37 CFR 1.196(b)(2); 1.197(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant may request rehearing of the Board's new rejection; the request must address the new ground and state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked and state all other grounds for rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceeding under rehearing waives the right to further prosecution before the examiner. A request for rehearing accompanied by an appropriate amendment or affidavit/declaration is not a proper 1.196(b)(2) rehearing request and will be treated as a submission under 1.196(b)(1). Requests for rehearing of an affirmance should be filed in a separate paper to facilitate consideration. The rule limits rehearing requests to points of law or fact believed overlooked, not mere reargument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limits and extensions for actions after Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Various time periods are prescribed: e.g., appellant generally has two months to act on a new ground of rejection or to request rehearing; requests for rehearing must be filed within two months of the original decision (single request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These two-month periods are non-extendable except under provisions of 37 CFR 1.136(b) (or 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination). The period for seeking court review of a Board decision is generally two months (with specified extensions under 37 CFR 1.304). Failure to act within prescribed periods may result in dismissal or termination of proceedings; examiners must take up applications when review periods lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing is a written-record proceeding (no entitlement to another oral hearing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'rehearing' means a rehearing on the written record, not an entitlement to an oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not normal practice to grant rehearings in the sense of another oral hearing; rehearing is limited to points specifically alleged as misapprehended or overlooked. Many rehearing petitions are mere reargument and are disfavored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure following Board decision — return to examiner and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After decision by the Board the application will be returned to the examiner, subject to appellant's right of appeal or other review, for such further action by appellant or examiner as required to carry the decision into effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the decision is mailed to appellant and the original placed in the file; the clerk notes the decision on the file wrapper and record of appeals and forwards the file to the examiner immediately if all rejections are reversed, or after about 10 weeks if any rejection is affirmed or after a rehearing decision is rendered. When a file is received after Board decision, it must be examined and precautions taken to indicate presence of allowed claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling cancelled or withdrawn claims after Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appellant withdraws some appealed claims and the Board reverses the examiner on remaining claims, the withdrawal is treated as an authorization to cancel the withdrawn claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary to notify the appellant of the cancellation of the withdrawn claims; the examiner may cancel withdrawn claims when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions when sustained in whole or in part (post-Board affirmance)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board affirms a rejection (in whole or part), various examiner actions may follow depending on claim relationships and what stands allowed or rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: if an independent claim is rejected and a dependent claim is allowed only because it depends on the rejected claim, examiner should either (1) convert dependent claim into independent form by examiner's amendment, cancel claims where rejection affirmed and issue application, or (2) set a one-month time limit for applicant to rewrite the dependent claim in independent form (no 1.136(a) extension). If no reply, cancel appropriate claims and issue application with the allowed claims only. Use suggested notice language (form paragraph 12.20). If uncorrected formal matters remain, take appropriate action but prosecution is otherwise closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings and consequences (37 CFR 1.197(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings are considered terminated by dismissal of an appeal or failure to timely file an appeal to court or civil action, except where claims stand allowed or nature of decision requires further examiner action; the date of termination is the date the appeal is dismissed or time to appeal expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If court review time (plus allowance for mail) has passed without review, the examiner must take up the application. If a civil action or appeal has been filed, proceedings are considered terminated when that action is terminated (e.g., receiving mandate). In ex parte reexamination, a reexamination certificate should be issued as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after Board decision (37 CFR 1.198)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases decided by the Board will not be reopened or reconsidered by the primary examiner except under the provisions of §1.114 or §1.196 and only with written authority of the Commissioner and for consideration of matters not already adjudicated, with sufficient cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening is tightly restricted: must have Commissioner authority and involve matters not adjudicated in prior decision; see 37 CFR 1.198.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public availability of Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of the Board may be published at the discretion of the Commissioner; requests to publish should be referred to the Office of the Solicitor. A decision in a pending or abandoned application will be published in accordance with 37 CFR 1.14(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board decisions that are open to the public are available in electronic form on the USPTO website; requests by members of the public or applicants to publish a decision are handled by the Office of the Solicitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner requests for rehearing of Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may request rehearing of a Board decision, normally within two months of receipt of the decision in the Technology Center (TC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests must be approved by the TC Director and forwarded to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for approval before mailing. The request should set a period of one month for the appellant to file a reply; if approved, the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy will mail a copy to the appellant and after reply period the file is forwarded to the Board.
